phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in the Holocene head of Daphnia magna

paleobiology.what_changes: Nothing changes along the age axis: the series is a single extant terminal at 0 Ma, so there is no predecessor chronospecies to inherit a wavelength from and no successor to pass one to. What changes is the length selected at this tier. The organelle-scale predecessor length is a screening-pigment melanosome near 0.5 µm. This tier selects the Turing wavenumber of a Schnakenberg field with λ_c = 2.736 µm. The cellular-scale successor length is an ommatidial pitch of tens of micrometres (Smith & Macagno 1990 resolve one ommatidium at a time). Slot 149's alpha/beta placeholders are a different model and are not reused.

equations.homogeneous_state: u0 = a + b,  v0 = b / (a + b)²
equations.jacobian: f_u = −1 + 2 u0 v0,  f_v = u0²,  g_u = −2 u0 v0,  g_v = −u0²
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c² = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.dispersion: σ(k) = ½ [tr(J − k²D) + sqrt(tr² − 4 det(J − k²D))]
equations.boundary_conditions: Periodic on a square pigment-epithelium patch. Length unit chosen so the analytical λ_c equals 2.736 µm.

empirical_claims.claim: A homogeneous chemical state can be unstable at a finite critical wavenumber k_c, selecting a wavelength λ_c = 2π/k_c.
The two-species mass-action system du/dt = a − u + u²v, dv/dt = b − u²v has a stable limit cycle in a well-mixed reactor and, with unequal diffusion, a Turing instability.

The visual system of Daphnia magna is assembled by cellular interactions; delaying optic-axon ingrowth delays laminar-neuron differentiation. This is pattern formation in the eye, not a measured pigment-stripe period.
Single ommatidia of Daphnia magna contain four spectral classes of photoreceptor. The ommatidium is the cellular-scale successor of the 2.736 µm field, not the field itself.
Cuticular melanin in Daphnia is an inducible shield against ultraviolet light. The paper does not report a 2.7 µm Turing wavelength.

specimen.description: Lateral SEM of the head of Daphnia magna, ×130, 100 µm scale bar.
